title: Livebook
name: livebook
description: Interactive Elixir notebooks saved as plain Markdown, with charts, tables, maps and forms built in, plus a way to turn a notebook into a small web app. Pulls in any Hex package from inside a notebook. Source: https://github.com/livebook-dev/livebook

env.name: LIVEBOOK_PASSWORD
env.label: Password (required)
env.description: What you'll log in with, 12 characters or more. Generate one with: openssl rand -hex 16

env.name: LIVEBOOK_SECRET_KEY_BASE
env.label: Secret key (required)
env.description: Signs your login, so it survives restarts and updates. Generate one with: openssl rand -base64 48

env.name: LIVEBOOK_PORT
env.label: Host port for the web UI

note: Set the password and secret key before you deploy, since the stack won't start without both. Then open http://<your-host>:8590 (or whichever port you picked) and log in. Charts and widgets load from port 8591 on the same host, so keep that one open too - it's fixed, and changing it breaks every output. Notebooks save to the livebook-notebooks volume (/data in the file picker), and settings live in livebook-config. Packages you pull in with Mix.install download again after an update, which is normal. Whoever logs in can run any code on the server, so keep it off the open internet unless it's behind HTTPS. Docs: hexdocs.pm/livebook
